notes: Capacity comparisons pair May 2025 pupil rolls with reported capacity as at 1 May 2025. They are a dated snapshot, not live vacancies or admissions guarantees.
The dataset covers mainstream state-funded primary-phase schools, including separate infant and junior schools. Nursery is excluded.
History uses May census counts in each academic year. Do not splice this series to the consultation leaflet, which uses different snapshots.
Nearby comparisons use the three schools in the council Kew planning area: Kew Riverside Primary School, Darell and The King’s (formerly The Queen’s).
Whole-school capacity is distinct from annual Reception admission numbers or temporary admission reductions. No claim is made about staffed or immediately available places.
SCAP net capacity excludes capacity in SEN units and resourced provision, which is collected separately. These comparisons do not establish suitable or available SEND provision.
January 2026 cohort totals sum full-time and part-time boys and girls within each curriculum year. These are year groups, not classes. Nursery is excluded.
January 2026 is not September 2026. Kew’s measured January total of 84 must not be confused with the separately published 2026/27 forecast of 84.
Thomson House’s two site rows are added to produce one school record. There are 46 raw sites/rows and 45 schools in each selected capacity year.

School histories retain source-year URNs and join by stable LAESTAB. Three schools changed URN over this period; names and LAESTAB remain continuous. No cross-year median-school comparison has been calculated.
Zero-sized year groups at separate infant or junior schools can mean the school does not offer that year; do not label these as empty classes. The three nearby schools all cover Reception to Year 6.
No suppressed or missing cells were converted to zero. All selected numerical cells are numeric and reconciled to source totals.
